- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward — overcorrecting or lagging in subsequent days.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when historical prices are trending upward.
- Mean reversion is under-estimated — model holds high forecasts longer than actual price tends to revert.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows increasing underestimation of late-period price peaks (last 5–10 days), suggesting model struggles with tail risk or momentum decay.
- Model often fails to adjust for recent downward momentum — continues to project upward trend even after price correction.
- When historical prices are volatile, model tends to smooth out extremes, leading to underestimation of volatility-driven price swings.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility spikes — forecasts peak too high and then fails to adjust downward quickly.
